subject: Burst isolation ops pathway + decision log
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@bioforge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps — Dedicated pool, burst isolation, SLA options

Hi Lina,

Thanks again for the time this morning — really helpful to see BioForge's production constraints and the latency/stability goals for your inference pipelines. Below is a short recap and a proposed ops pathway we discussed. I put expected owners and a decision log at the bottom so we can lock things quickly.

Key pain points you shared
- Model inference variance during peak analysis windows (15–30% higher p99) that spikes cost.
- Regulatory requirement to silo sensitive patient models (must run in a VPC-dedicated pool).
- Need for predictable throughput for nightly batch runs while preserving sub-100ms online latency for interactive tools.

Goals we aligned on
- Dedicated reserved pool (initial 4x A100-equivalent slots) with hard isolation for regulated models.
- Burst capacity to handle 2–3x overnight batch throughput for 3 hours without impacting online SLOs.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime, p99 latency < 120ms for online routes, and a clear fallback plan to lower-cost variants if capacity is constrained.

Proposed ops pathway (high level)
1) Reserve: Contract for a 4-slot dedicated pool (monthly reservation) + defined burst budget.
2) Isolation: Separate VPC pool for sensitive models; KV/prefix caching enabled to avoid cold-starts during bursts.
3) Scaling: Autoscale policy with pre-warm window (15 minutes) + controlled queued burst to preserve online SLOs.
4) Fallbacks: Policy mapping to quantized model variant (Q4) for batch-only routes.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-term-sheet-v1.pdf (term sheet with pricing tiers), isolation-diagram.png (network segmentation sketch).

Immediate asks / next steps
- Lina: confirm target start date for reserved pool + preferred billing cadence (monthly vs annual) — by EOD Tue.
- BioForge procurement: share any template clause that would block VPC onboarding (security/SC-clauses) — CC'd procurement email works.
- Marissa / Aditya: prepare SOW draft and preliminary sizing runbook (internal).

Decision log (so far)
- Isolation required: YES (must be VPC dedicated).
- Initial reserved size: PROVISIONAL 4x slots, subject to sizing run.

Happy to jump on another 30m if it's helpful.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive – Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Lina Gomez <lina@bioforge.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, procurement@bioforge.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Dedicated pool, burst isolation, SLA options

Naomi — thanks for the crisp recap. Confirming the points below and a couple clarifications:

- Isolation: confirmed, BioForge legal requires a dedicated VPC and monthly audit logs (retain 12 months).
- Initial sizing: 4 slots acceptable as a starting point; we expect to need +1 slot within 6 weeks if nightly batch execution increases as forecasted.
- Burst: We prefer a guaranteed burst window with soft throttling after burst budget is exhausted (rather than immediate fallback to a quantized variant). We do want an ordered fallback ladder though (quantized variant -> regional fallbacks).

Procurement has been looped in (procurement@bioforge.ai) — they asked for your standard term sheet and a vendor security questionnaire (SOC2 section). I'll get them to send our PO template if the numbers align.

Would like a short ops call next Tue (30m) with your infra lead to confirm pre-warm windows and KV cache behavior.

Thanks,
Lina
Head of ML Ops, BioForge
Lina@bioforge.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Term sheet + SOC2 next steps / DocuSign

Procurement team,

Thanks for the prompt attention. Attaching the term sheet (redwood-dedicated-term-sheet-v1.pdf) which includes: reserved capacity pricing for 4-slot pool, burst credits pricing, and an SLA appendix for 99.9% uptime and p99 latency guardrails.

I've also opened a DocuSign envelope for a mutual NDA and initial reservation addendum to accelerate the pilot onboarding. Link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-redwood-bioforge (please let me know if procurement prefers a different routing).

Marissa / Aditya — please review the attached term sheet and push a preliminary SOW + one-page runbook to the shared Drive link (https://drive.redwood-internal.com/teams/sales/bioforge/ops-playbook). Goal: internal draft by Monday so procurement has clear deliverables for the PO.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Decision log + owners (BioForge)

Quick internal note to capture owners and open items after Lina's confirmation:

Owners
- Contract & Pricing: Naomi (primary) / Marissa (support)
- SOW + Runbook: Marissa (create draft) / Infra (Aditya to review pre-warm & cache params)
- Security Questionnaires: Naomi to coordinate, Infra to provide SOC2 evidence snippets (logs retention, KMS outline)

Open items / Risks
- Risk: BioForge wants burst behavior that delays quantized fallbacks; need to confirm that long bursts won't degrade online p99 for interactive routes. Action: Aditya to run a short simulation and propose a burst throttling curve by Mon EOD.
- Risk: PO cadence — they asked monthly vs annual. Monthly increases churn risk; include 10% uplift on monthly vs annual pricing in SOW to keep economics tight.

Draft deliverables (timeline)
- Mon 26 Apr: Internal SOW + runbook draft (Marissa)
- Tue 27 Apr: Ops call with BioForge infra (Aditya + Naomi)
- Wed 28 Apr: Procurement gets DocuSign back, PO template review

I'll track the decision log in HubSpot (link above). File the runbook to the Drive folder and I'll pull the network diagram into the SOW appendix.

-Marissa
Account Executive (Solutions) — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
